open_items: ESTAT list_dataflows timeout pattern: nineteenth episode, cycle 374 only, resolved by cycle 375, clean through cycle 379. Consistent with the usual one-cycle recovery (only the eighteenth episode, cycles 362-364, persisted beyond one cycle). Watch for a twentieth episode, and specifically whether multi-cycle persistence recurs. Standing recommendation (raise deadline, stream listing, or cache parsed result) remains open as a code-change-scope fix, not actioned by this read-only routine.

ILO gateway-data-only 403 flap (standalone): two occurrences on record, cycle 370 (resolved by 371) and cycle 322 (tail end of the cycle 321 blanket-403 episode). Both resolved within one to two cycles. No new occurrence through cycle 379. Watch for a third occurrence, and specifically whether it ever persists past one cycle.

ABS gateway metadata empty-error-body flap: tenth occurrence at cycle 365, resolved by cycle 366. All ten occurrences have resolved within one cycle. No new occurrence through cycle 379. Empty error message itself still worth fixing under code-change scope (GatewayError/next_step in monitor/checks_gateway.py).

SBS gateway DNS resolution flap: first occurrence, cycle 366 (`Temporary failure in name resolution` on gateway metadata, gateway data probe timed out), resolved by cycle 367. No second occurrence through cycle 379. Isolated to SBS; same failure shape previously seen for FBOS at cycle 50 (treated as infrastructure, not provider-down). Watch for a second occurrence; escalate if it recurs.

UNICEF HTTP 429 flap: sixth occurrence cycle 346, resolved by cycle 347. Prior occurrences cycle 126, 178, 262, 305, 346, all resolved within one cycle. No new occurrence through cycle 379. Watch for a seventh occurrence.

ILO blanket-403 provider_down episode: seventh occurrence cycle 321 (priors: 244, 251, 260, 264, 272, 281, all resolved within one cycle). This one took two cycles instead of one -- gateway_issue at 322 (gateway data probe only), fully healthy by 323. No new occurrence through cycle 379 (the cycle 370 gateway-data-only 403 is a separate standalone occurrence of a similar shape, not a recurrence of the blanket 403 itself). Watch for an eighth blanket-403 occurrence, and specifically whether a staggered recovery repeats or was a one-off.

ABS and ESTAT gateway_issue coincided in the same cycle (319) for the first time on record. Each pattern is independently well established; could not determine whether this reflects a shared cause or is coincidence. No second simultaneous occurrence through cycle 379. Watch for a second true same-cycle occurrence.

OECD gateway_issue 403 Forbidden episode (cycles 290-292, gateway list_dataflows and gateway data probe both HTTP 403, direct path healthy throughout): resolved by cycle 293. No new occurrence through cycle 379. First occurrence of this pattern for OECD, notable for spanning three consecutive cycles (~6h). Watch for a second occurrence; escalate for real if a future episode again spans more than one cycle.

ILO direct-path 403 flap (basic checks): tenth occurrence cycle 286, resolved by cycle 287 (one cycle, as usual), clean since (superseded by the blanket 403 at cycle 321, a different and more severe pattern -- see above). Prior occurrences cycle 32, 94, 159, 166, 202, 238, 244, 249, 267. Watch for an eleventh occurrence of this specific direct-only shape.

ILO references:contentconstraint broken (500) at cycle 274 resolved by cycle 275 (reads `ignored`, not `broken`, in the current cycle's contract rows). Second occurrence overall of this assertion flapping (first was a same-cycle blip at cycle 199). No new occurrence through cycle 379. Watch for a third occurrence; escalate if a future broken reading persists beyond one cycle.

ILO gateway_issue episode (cycles 268-269, gateway metadata HTTP 500 on list_dataflows, direct healthy throughout): resolved by cycle 270. No new occurrence through cycle 379. Distinct pattern from the cycle 322 and cycle 370 gateway data 403 episodes (see above): different check (metadata vs data) and different HTTP status (500 vs 403). Watch separately.

ECB contract-probe 504 flap (second pattern): constraint:availableconstraint (504 -> 404) and references:none (504 -> 200) both showed a was/now change in /api/contracts between cycle 283 and 286, verdict stayed ok throughout. No further changes list entries on these assertions through cycle 379. Not the same assertions as the cycles 182-183 references:* 504 flap (that watch item is separate, still clean). Watch for recurrence on these two assertions specifically.
